The flagship for news around the universe. Adults 21+. For entertainment purposes only.

## 2026-10-25 04:13 UTC
1. PR Newswire | Quantinuum achieved a world-record logical fidelity of 99.9995 percent on its Helios system, five errors per million operations, 10 times better than its September record and 100 times better than the best published result from other hardware — error correction now in the target range for its planned Apollo fault-tolerant computer by 2029.
2. BitRss | Google's latest quantum results sparked renewed urgency for post-quantum migration in crypto, with analysts warning dormant Bitcoin outputs and fast-clock quantum architectures could make on-spend attacks feasible sooner and Ethereum targeting 2029 readiness while Bitcoin's path remains fragmented — migration planning for wallets and chains can no longer wait.
3. Sky News | Brazilians voted Sunday in a presidential runoff between incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro, neck-and-neck after a hard-fought campaign — the result deciding whether Latin America's largest country stays left or shifts right with US backing.
4. Wall Street Next | US inflation climbed to 3.7 percent year-over-year in September as gasoline jumped 9.1 percent in a month and accounted for over half the monthly CPI rise, Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed — energy disruption tied to the Iran conflict complicating the Federal Reserve's next rate decision.
5. USGS | A magnitude 7.2 earthquake off Vanuatu, later revised to 6.9, with a second 6.3 quake nearby, triggered a tsunami warning that was later cancelled — the Ring of Fire archipelago again exposed to major seismic risk.
6. New York Post | Protests gripping France spread Saturday across Europe, with demonstrators clashing with police in Albania and Brussels, water cannons deployed in Tirana, and Italy putting Milan on high alert with soldiers and drone surveillance — a continent-wide wave over living costs and government.
7. NASA | NASA's James Webb Space Telescope confirmed a supernova that exploded when the universe was only 730 million years old, the earliest stellar death ever observed, breaking Webb's previous 1.8-billion-year record — and its spectrum looks surprisingly like modern supernovae, so local tools apply across most of cosmic history.
8. ANI | President Donald Trump, voting in Palm Beach, said the United States will do business with both Ukraine and Russia after the war ends and hoped for a deal, while First Lady Melania Trump pointed to Vatican support and the October 27 ceasefire timeline — Washington framing post-war commerce alongside the truce effort.
9. WiseVoter | The United States recorded a $1.992 trillion federal deficit for fiscal year 2026 as Senator Rick Scott proposed spending cuts and deregulation to curb inflation — the deficit scale sharpening the debate over energy production and federal spending ahead of the midterms.
10. Le Monde | Israel's Haaretz newspaper is fighting government pressure ahead of crucial elections, with authorities accusing the critical outlet of treason amid mass protests — a press-freedom test for democratic institutions during a contested vote.
11. Al Jazeera | Bulgarians voted for president in the shadow of Russia's war in Ukraine, with leading candidates condemning deadly Black Sea drone strikes while differing on the war's course — European allies watching for signals on regional stability.
12. NASA | A 100-hour observation with a special oxygen filter revealed three previously unknown nebulas near Gamma Cassiopeiae, blue phantoms alongside the Ghosts of Cassiopeia IC 59 and IC 63 — their origins, possibly a bow shock or a planetary nebula, remain unsolved.
13. Disclosure News | Bavarian police detained a 33-year-old German man after a fire engulfed the Kehlsteinhaus, Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat above Berchtesgaden, with prosecutors saying a political motive has not been ruled out and the investigation is in early stages.

1. Axios | US intelligence warned Iranian plots to kill Americans abroad have reached advanced stages, in an October 23 memorandum from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, as Washington reduces staffing at embassies in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the UAE — a threat picture driving diplomatic drawdowns across the Middle East.

3. 5. 6. Financial Times | Forty-seven large data centre projects have already fallen through this year and analysts at Bernstein believe only about 35 percent of planned facilities are feasible, the Financial Times reported — a sharp feasibility gap in the AI infrastructure build-out even as demand forecasts keep rising.

8. CNN | Iowa's rising cancer rates, against a national decline, are scrambling one of the country's most competitive Senate races, CNN reported, with a Democratic super PAC spending nearly $3 million since September on the issue and a divide over the herbicide glyphosate splitting farmers from the MAHA movement.

10. Morning Briefing | Agent cloud startup Daytona reached a $1 billion valuation on a $60 million Series B led by FirstMark, the October 24 Morning Briefing reported — cloud infrastructure built specifically for AI agents reaching unicorn status as agent workloads become a distinct computing market.
11. ScienceDaily | Samples from asteroid Bennu collected by NASA are revealing new details about how the solar system formed about 4.5 billion years ago, with a new chemical analysis challenging earlier theories about the asteroid's birthplace, ScienceDaily reported.
12. Okay News | JPMorgan has received initial regulatory approval for a Nigerian merchant bank, Okay News reported — an early step, not yet an operating institution, toward a major US bank's formal entry into Africa's most populous economy.
13. BBC News | Two Israeli soldiers were killed Friday morning when two Palestinian gunmen attacked a checkpoint outside a West Bank city, BBC News and JNS reported — lethal violence continuing days before Israel's general election.

11. Guardian | Israel is heading to the polls deeply divided, the Guardian reported, with former military chief Gadi Eisenkot challenging Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and voters in southern Lebanon doubting the result will change the occupation — an election framed as a referendum on Netanyahu.

1. 7. Deccan Herald | The United States has for years asked Elon Musk to alter Starlink service in Ukraine and the Middle East, sources said — a satellite network privately controlled yet repeatedly treated as an instrument of state policy in active conflicts.
8. Polish Press Agency | Poland does not have enough Patriot air defence missiles to hand over to Ukraine, Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski told the Polish Press Agency, warning Russia is producing more missiles than the West has interceptors to neutralise them and urging other NATO members to supply the scarce systems.

10. Euronews | The European Investment Bank will double its climate funding to 30 billion euros as extreme weather costs soar, Euronews reported — a shift from climate mitigation toward economic protection against climate damage.

12. Cosmic Herald | Five years after launch, NASA's Lucy spacecraft is under a year from its first Jupiter Trojan asteroid, Eurybates, on August 12, 2027 — the first close look at a population of early solar system remnants no spacecraft has ever visited.
13. Russian Defence Ministry | Ukraine and Russia swapped 270 servicemen each in a prisoner exchange on Friday, the first since August, which President Volodymyr Zelenskiy called a very important result, as a US-brokered ceasefire in the occupied town of Oleshky is set to take effect October 27 with technical peace talks scheduled for Abu Dhabi in November.

5. NewzTodays | Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5 designed quantum circuits that cut gate counts by up to 17 times across eight benchmark tasks, including a first reversible elliptic-curve point addition circuit built over 53 hours with minimal human intervention — AI now directly shrinking the resource cost of quantum algorithms.
6. Barchart | Google said its magic state cultivation technique cut errors roughly 40-fold on its Willow quantum processor and reached 99.99 percent logical fidelity for a critical quantum state, in results published in Science — tackling a bottleneck between experimental machines and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

10. GlobeNewswire | Quantum X Labs said its quantum error-correction decoder, now running on NVIDIA CUDA-Q, made 12 to 13 percent fewer logical errors than the standard PyMatching decoder on Google's public quantum hardware data, while its LayerQake work cut maximum cumulative error 15- to 21-fold across three IBM processors.
11. Daily Galaxy | NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope entered science commissioning on October 22, with NASA confirming the observatory is fully functional and final tests now refining image quality — the wide-field survey telescope set to uncover millions of hidden cosmic objects.
